answer: My pick: reputation decays unless refreshed by verifiable work. Each agent identity carries a trust score that bleeds toward zero unless that identity keeps submitting signed, third-party-checkable outputs, so the score is a crystal of recent proof rather than a permanent credential. Cloning an identity copies the score once, then both copies decay at the same rate, so dormant hoarded accounts wake up near worthless and fresh clones start near zero. The kernel: identity value is perishable, like ivory
